ap_chemistry::Mass spectrum of a single.title: Mass spectrum of a single element
ap_chemistry::Mass spectrum of a single.body: A graph of relative abundance versus mass for the isotopes of one element.
ap_chemistry::Mass spectrum of a single.caution: Isotopes of one element differ in mass because they have different numbers of neutrons, not different numbers of protons or electrons. Read the y-axis scale carefully when estimating abundances.

items.label: Peak position (x-axis)
items.meaning: Mass of an isotope, which identifies the isotope

items.label: Peak height (y-axis)
items.meaning: Relative abundance of that isotope in nature

ap_chemistry::Photoelectron spectrum (PE.title: Photoelectron spectrum (PES)
ap_chemistry::Photoelectron spectrum (PE.body: A plot of peaks, one per subshell, used to relate the spectrum to electron configuration and electron-nucleus interactions.

items.label: Peak position
items.meaning: Energy required to remove an electron from the corresponding subshell

items.label: Relative peak height
items.meaning: Ideally proportional to the number of electrons in that subshell

ap_chemistry::Potential energy vs. inter.title: Potential energy vs. internuclear distance graph
ap_chemistry::Potential energy vs. inter.body: Graph of potential energy versus the distance between two atoms, used to describe the interaction between the atoms, with the lowest-energy point marking the equilibrium bond length and the bond energy read from the energy needed to separate the atoms.

items.label: Vertical axis: potential energy
items.meaning: Potential energy of the pair of interacting atoms.

items.label: Horizontal axis: internuclear distance
items.meaning: Distance between the nuclei of the two atoms.

items.label: Lowest point of the curve
items.meaning: Equilibrium bond length: the separation between atoms at which the potential energy is lowest.

items.label: Depth of the energy well
items.meaning: Bond energy: the energy required to separate the atoms.

items.label: Effect of bond order
items.meaning: Bonds with a higher order (single, double, triple) are shorter and have larger bond energies.

ap_chemistry::Sea-of-electrons model of.title: Sea-of-electrons model of metallic bonding
ap_chemistry::Sea-of-electrons model of.body: A metallic solid is drawn as an array of positive metal ions surrounded by delocalized valence electrons.

items.label: Positive metal ions
items.meaning: Cores of the metal atoms arranged in an array.

items.label: Delocalized valence electrons
items.meaning: The "sea of electrons" surrounding the ions, not tied to any one atom.

ap_chemistry::Particulate model of solid.title: Particulate model of solid, liquid, and gas
ap_chemistry::Particulate model of solid.body: A particulate-level model shows how particle arrangement, spacing, and motion differ among the solid, liquid, and gas phases.

items.label: Solid (crystalline or amorphous)
items.meaning: Particles are in close contact. They are in a regular 3-D arrangement if crystalline and an irregular one if amorphous. Motion is limited, with no overall translation of particles relative to each other.

items.label: Liquid
items.meaning: Particles are in close contact, similar in molar volume to the solid, and are continually moving and colliding. Their arrangement and movement depend on the nature and strength of the forces between them.

items.label: Gas
items.meaning: Particles are in constant motion with minimal effects from forces between them. Collision frequency and average spacing depend on temperature, pressure, and volume. The gas has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.

ap_chemistry::Particulate representation.title: Particulate representation of a solution
ap_chemistry::Particulate representation.body: A particulate model of a solution communicates its structure and properties by showing the interactions among components and the relative concentrations of components.

items.label: Interactions between components
items.meaning: Drawings that show the interactions among the solute and solvent components.

items.label: Concentrations of components
items.meaning: The relative numbers of particles of each component in the solution.

ap_chemistry::Particulate representation.title: Particulate representation of a balanced equation
ap_chemistry::Particulate representation.body: A balanced equation in any form can be translated into a consistent particulate model.

items.label: Reactant particles
items.meaning: Particles shown before the change

items.label: Product particles
items.meaning: Particles shown after the change

items.label: Atom conservation
items.meaning: Equal numbers of atoms of each element before and after

ap_chemistry::Maxwell-Boltzmann energy d.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution
ap_chemistry::Maxwell-Boltzmann energy d.body: A distribution curve of particle energies, used to gain a qualitative estimate of the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to react and how that fraction depends on temperature.
ap_chemistry::Maxwell-Boltzmann energy d.caution: The CED treats this as a qualitative estimate only. Energy alone is not enough, because successful collisions also need a suitable orientation.

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: particle energy

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: relative number (fraction) of particles having each energy

items.label: Distribution curve
items.meaning: describes the distribution of particle energies at a given temperature

items.label: Activation energy marker
items.meaning: a vertical line on the energy axis; particles at or above it have sufficient energy to overcome the activation energy

items.label: Area beyond the marker
items.meaning: qualitative estimate of the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to lead to a reaction

items.label: Curves at different temperatures
items.meaning: show how the fraction of sufficiently energetic particles depends on temperature

ap_chemistry::Single-step reaction energ.title: Single-step reaction energy profile
ap_chemistry::Single-step reaction energ.body: A plot of energy along the reaction coordinate from reactants, through a transition state, to products.

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Energy

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Reaction coordinate

items.label: Reactants
items.meaning: Starting energy level

items.label: Transition state
items.meaning: Energy maximum between reactants and products

items.label: Products
items.meaning: Ending energy level

items.label: Activation energy
items.meaning: Energy difference from reactants to transition state (forward reaction)

items.label: Overall energy change
items.meaning: Energy difference between products and reactants

ap_chemistry::Multistep reaction energy.title: Multistep reaction energy profile
ap_chemistry::Multistep reaction energy.body: An energy profile for a multistep mechanism built from the energetics of each elementary step.

items.label: Reaction coordinate axis
items.meaning: Horizontal axis spanning all steps

items.label: Transition state for each step
items.meaning: An energy maximum for each elementary step

items.label: Activation energy for each step
items.meaning: Barrier from that step's starting level to its transition state

items.label: Reaction intermediate(s)
items.meaning: Species between steps, at energies between transition states

items.label: Overall energy change
items.meaning: Energy of final products relative to initial reactants

ap_chemistry::Energy diagram for a physi.title: Energy diagram for a physical or chemical process
ap_chemistry::Energy diagram for a physi.body: A diagram that shows whether a process is endothermic or exothermic by comparing the energy of the starting and ending states.

items.label: Energy axis
items.meaning: The vertical axis, labelled with energy and units.

items.label: Reactants (initial state) level
items.meaning: Energy of the system before the process.

items.label: Products (final state) level
items.meaning: Energy of the system after the process.

items.label: Direction of change
items.meaning: Products lower than reactants means exothermic; products higher means endothermic.

ap_chemistry::Graphs showing the approac.title: Graphs showing the approach to equilibrium
ap_chemistry::Graphs showing the approac.body: Concentration, partial pressure, or rate versus time graphs used to show how equilibrium is established.

items.label: Concentration or partial pressure vs. time
items.meaning: Reactant and product curves change, then level off to constant values once equilibrium is reached

items.label: Rate vs. time
items.meaning: Forward rate and reverse rate approach each other and become equal at equilibrium

items.label: Constant region
items.meaning: Flat lines indicate no net change, although both processes continue

ap_chemistry::Particulate model of a rev.title: Particulate model of a reversible reaction
ap_chemistry::Particulate model of a rev.body: A particulate diagram shows the relative numbers of reactant and product particles before and at equilibrium, and from these the value of the equilibrium constant.

items.label: Prior to equilibrium
items.meaning: Relative numbers of reactant and product particles in the initial mixture.

items.label: At equilibrium
items.meaning: Relative numbers of reactant and product particles present once the forward and reverse rates are equal.

items.label: Equilibrium constant
items.meaning: K is found from the particle counts at equilibrium, using the same form as the K expression.

ap_chemistry::Titration curve (pH vs. vo.title: Titration curve (pH vs. volume of titrant)
ap_chemistry::Titration curve (pH vs. vo.body: A titration curve plots pH against the volume of titrant added and summarizes results from a titration; students read it to find the equivalence point and, for weak acids/bases, the half-equivalence point.
ap_chemistry::Titration curve (pH vs. vo.caution: Do not confuse the half-equivalence point (pH = pKa) with the equivalence point; pKa is read from the pH at the half-equivalence point, not the equivalence point.

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: pH

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: volume of titrant added

items.label: Equivalence point
items.meaning: moles of titrant added equal moles of analyte originally present (monoprotic acids or bases); pH is set by the major species present (neutral for strong acid-strong base; basic for a weak acid titration, acidic for a weak base titration)

items.label: Half-equivalence point
items.meaning: for a weak acid, the point halfway to the equivalence point where [HA] = [A−], so pH = pKa

ap_chemistry::Electrochemical cell diagr.title: Electrochemical cell diagram
ap_chemistry::Electrochemical cell diagr.body: Cell diagrams are read to identify where each half-reaction occurs, the direction of current and electron flow, and the cell type; each component has a specific role.

items.label: Electrodes
items.meaning: Anode (oxidation) and cathode (reduction); mass change or gas evolution can occur at an electrode

items.label: Half-cell solutions
items.meaning: Contain the active species of each half-reaction

items.label: Salt bridge
items.meaning: Allows ion flow between half-cells

items.label: Voltage/current measuring device
items.meaning: Measures cell potential or current

ap_statistics::Bar chart.title: Bar chart
ap_statistics::Bar chart.body: Each bar is one category of a single categorical variable, and bar height or length shows its frequency or relative frequency.

items.label: Bar
items.meaning: one category of the categorical variable

items.label: Bar height/length
items.meaning: frequency (count) or relative frequency (proportion) of units in that category

ap_statistics::Boxplot.title: Boxplot
ap_statistics::Boxplot.body: A boxplot is a graph of the five-number summary, with a box spanning Q1 to Q3, a line at the median, whiskers to the extreme non-outlier values, and outliers marked separately.

items.label: Box
items.meaning: Represents the middle 50% of the data, with ends at Q1 and Q3

items.label: Median line
items.meaning: Line inside the box at the median

items.label: Whiskers
items.meaning: Lines representing 25% of the data each, extending from Q1 to the minimum and from Q3 to the maximum

items.label: Whisker ends when outliers exist
items.meaning: The whiskers extend to the most extreme data values that are not outliers

items.label: Outliers
items.meaning: Usually denoted with an asterisk or other symbol

ap_statistics::Dotplot.title: Dotplot
ap_statistics::Dotplot.body: Each observation is a dot placed above (or beside) its value on the axis, with nearly identical values stacked.

items.label: Dot
items.meaning: one observation of the quantitative variable

items.label: Axis position
items.meaning: the value of that observation

items.label: Stacking
items.meaning: nearly identical values are stacked on top of each other

ap_statistics::Graphs for two categorica.title: Graphs for two categorical variables
ap_statistics::Graphs for two categorica.body: Three graphs display the relationship between two categorical variables by showing the frequency or relative frequency of each level of one variable within each category of the other.

items.label: Side-by-side bar chart
items.meaning: Bars for the levels of one variable are shown for each category of the other variable.

items.label: Segmented bar chart
items.meaning: One bar per category of a variable, divided into segments for the levels of the other variable.

items.label: Mosaic plot
items.meaning: Displays the frequency or relative frequency of each level of one variable across the categories of the other variable.

ap_statistics::Histogram.title: Histogram
ap_statistics::Histogram.body: Ordered bins of the quantitative variable lie along the horizontal axis, and each bar's height is the frequency or relative frequency in that bin.

items.label: Bins (intervals)
items.meaning: ordered intervals of values along the horizontal axis (or vertical axis in a horizontal histogram)

items.label: Bar height
items.meaning: frequency or relative frequency of observations in the bin

items.label: Bin width
items.meaning: changing it can change the histogram's appearance

ap_statistics::Pie chart.title: Pie chart
ap_statistics::Pie chart.body: Each slice is one category, and its share of the total area is that category's relative frequency; all slices sum to 100%.

items.label: Slice
items.meaning: one category of the categorical variable

items.label: Slice area as a fraction of total area
items.meaning: relative frequency of that category

items.label: All slices together
items.meaning: 1, or 100% of the total area

ap_statistics::Stem-and-leaf plot.title: Stem-and-leaf plot
ap_statistics::Stem-and-leaf plot.body: Each value is split into a stem (first digit or digits) and a leaf (usually the single digit after the stem), with both ordered smallest to largest.

items.label: Stem
items.meaning: first digit or digits of the value

items.label: Leaf
items.meaning: usually the single digit after the stem digit(s)

items.label: Ordering
items.meaning: stems and leaves both ordered smallest to largest

ap_physics_2::Graph of electric potentia.title: Graph of electric potential versus position in a loop
ap_physics_2::Graph of electric potentia.body: A graph showing the electric potential at points in a circuit as a function of position within a loop.

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Position within the loop

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Electric potential

items.label: Changes along the graph
items.meaning: Potential differences across each circuit element

items.label: End of loop
items.meaning: Net change in potential around the closed loop is zero

ap_physics_2::Maxwell–Boltzmann distribu.title: Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution (qualitative)
ap_physics_2::Maxwell–Boltzmann distribu.body: A graph of the energies or speeds of atoms at a given temperature; students relate its features to temperature but need not know its functional form.

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Atomic speed or energy

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Relative number of atoms at each speed or energy

items.label: Curve features
items.meaning: Features of the curve are related to the gas temperature

ap_physics_2::Pressure–volume (PV) diagr.title: Pressure–volume (PV) diagram
ap_physics_2::Pressure–volume (PV) diagr.body: A graph of pressure versus volume that represents a thermodynamic process, where the area under the curve gives the absolute value of the work done on or by the gas.
ap_physics_2::Pressure–volume (PV) diagr.caution: Area under the curve gives only the absolute value of the work. Determine the sign of W from whether the gas is compressed (work done on the gas, W > 0) or expanded (W < 0).

items.label: Vertical axis
items.meaning: Pressure P of the gas

items.label: Horizontal axis
items.meaning: Volume V of the gas

items.label: Area under the curve
items.meaning: Absolute value of the work done on the gas when it expands or compresses

items.label: Isotherm
items.meaning: A line of constant temperature on the PV diagram

items.label: Isovolumetric process
items.meaning: Constant volume

items.label: Isobaric process
items.meaning: Constant pressure

items.label: Isothermal process
items.meaning: Constant temperature

items.label: Adiabatic process
items.meaning: No energy transferred to or from the system through thermal processes

ap_physics_c_mechanics::Reading x(t), v(.title: Reading x(t), v(t), a(t) graphs
ap_physics_c_mechanics::Reading x(t), v(.body: Relationships among position, velocity, and acceleration graphs as functions of time.

items.label: Slope of tangent on x–t graph
items.meaning: Instantaneous velocity, v_x = dx/dt

items.label: Slope of tangent on v–t graph
items.meaning: Instantaneous acceleration, a_x = dv_x/dt

items.label: Area under v–t curve
items.meaning: Displacement during the interval

items.label: Area under a–t curve
items.meaning: Change in velocity during the interval

ap_precalculus::Residual plot.title: Residual plot
ap_precalculus::Residual plot.body: A residual plot graphs the residuals of a regression (actual dependent value minus the value predicted by the model) on the vertical axis against the independent variable on the horizontal axis, and a model is justified as appropriate if the plot appears without pattern.

ap_physics_c_mechanics::Change in veloci.title: Change in velocity from area under a–t graph

ap_physics_c_mechanics::Displacement fro.title: Displacement from area under v–t graph

ap_chemistry::How a catalyst increases r.title: How a catalyst increases rate
ap_chemistry::How a catalyst increases r.body: A catalyst must increase the number of effective collisions and/or provide a reaction path with a lower activation energy relative to the original reaction coordinate.
ap_chemistry::How a catalyst increases r.caution: A complete answer cites the specific effect (more effective collisions or an alternate lower-Ea path), not just 'it speeds up the reaction'.

ap_chemistry::Maxwell-Boltzmann distribu.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution
ap_chemistry::Maxwell-Boltzmann distribu.body: A graphical representation of the distribution of particle kinetic energies (or velocities) at a given temperature.

ap_physics_1::Slope and area relationshi.title: Slope and area relationships on motion graphs
ap_physics_1::Slope and area relationshi.body: How position, velocity, and acceleration graphs relate to each other.

items.label: Slope of tangent on x vs. t
items.meaning: Instantaneous velocity

items.label: Slope of tangent on v vs. t
items.meaning: Instantaneous acceleration

items.label: Area under v vs. t
items.meaning: Displacement during the interval

items.label: Area under a vs. t
items.meaning: Change in velocity during the interval

ap_physics_2::Ohmic materials and the I–.title: Ohmic materials and the I–ΔV graph
ap_physics_2::Ohmic materials and the I–.body: Ohmic materials have constant resistance for all currents, and the resistance of an ohmic element is found from the slope of its graph of current versus potential difference.
ap_physics_2::Ohmic materials and the I–.caution: On a graph of I (vertical) versus ΔV (horizontal), the slope equals 1/R, not R.

ap_physics_c_mechanics::Work as area und.title: Work as area under an F∥ vs. displacement graph
ap_physics_c_mechanics::Work as area und.body: Work equals the area under the curve of a graph of F∥ as a function of displacement.

ap_physics_1::Work from a force-displace.title: Work from a force-displacement graph
ap_physics_1::Work from a force-displace.body: Work equals the area under the curve of a graph of F (parallel component) as a function of displacement.

ap_physics_2::Zero-pressure temperature.title: Zero-pressure temperature from a P–T graph
ap_physics_2::Zero-pressure temperature.body: The temperature at which an ideal gas has zero pressure is found by extrapolating a graph of pressure as a function of temperature.

_note: Published app.unit_reference_entries rows (kind='diagram', subject ap_chemistry) in PRODUCTION (pcntajvbdfqhbeewmdry), read 2026-10-10; items[] restored 2026-10-11. Each entry's items[] is the exact published array: it was selected from this repository's batch candidate artifacts by matching md5(label»meaning joined on '|') against the same digest computed in Production, so no content was retyped. items_md5 records that digest; re-run the Production query in FIGURE_PRODUCTION_PROTOCOL.md section 2 to re-confirm. verify.py asserts label coverage per ENTRY against these arrays, so stripping them silently voids that gate. EXTENDED 2026-10-11: every entry now carries its published `body` (and `caution` where set) and a `body_md5`, because ced_check.py puts the body in the reader prompt as the entry's claim and it was resolving to '(not available)'. DECISION-0116 makes that prompt the only gate standing where the reference-pack checkers do not watch, so a route-(b) figure cannot be reviewed without it. The twelve AP Statistics and Physics entries added in the later batches carried no items_md5 at all; all 36 were re-read from Production on 2026-10-11, their stored items[] compared byte for byte (none had drifted), and the digests recorded. KEYED BY SUBJECT 2026-10-11: the key is now 'subject_key::title'. Two published entries share the title 'Vector arrow representation' -- AP Physics 1 1.1 and AP Physics C Mechanics 1.1 -- so a title-only key silently dropped one of them and the coverage gate would have asserted the survivor's items[] for both.
